counterfactual_missing_items: weak clonal band in a polyclonal background
decisive_items: history of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks prior to the development of the current eruption at the same site.
Dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes in the upper dermis
Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement
response.rationale: C1 uniquely integrates the site-specific HSV-2 antecedent with the atypical CD4+ infiltrate and non-clonal molecular profile, giving a complete pseudolymphoma mechanism. R5 is contradicted by the repeat negative clonality and weak polyclonal background; R3 lacks CD30/self-healing papules; R7 ignores the atypical infiltrate and firm nodules. R6 is the same diagnosis but omits the causal HSV-2 link.

rejected.why: Presumed chronic dermatitis was the initial clinical impression, but smooth firm nodules and atypical CD4+ infiltrate contradict dermatitis.
CTCL is undermined by the weak clonal band in a polyclonal background and repeat molecular studies showing no clonal rearrangement.
Lymphomatoid papulosis is unlikely without CD30+ atypical cells or self-healing papules; persistent plaques/nodules at the HSV-2 site favor pseudolymphoma.
